title: Lay a nickel strip on a 2x2 18650 battery pack and spot-weld it to all four cells
instruction: With your right gripper, lay the nickel strip flat on top of the battery pack with its bars over the cells, let go and move that arm back. Then, with your left gripper, take the spot welder out of its orange holder, spot-weld the strip to each of the four cells, put the welder back in its holder and move the left arm back too.
context: Joining cells into packs is regular work for team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00; with other miscellaneous assemblers, about 1.4 million US jobs, BLS), who rotate through every task of their line and assemble electrical equipment, and for electrical and electronic equipment assemblers (O*NET 51-2022.00), whose core task installs components "using rivets, bolts, soldering or micro-welding equipment", batteries among what they build. On lithium-ion pack lines and repair benches that means laying nickel strip over the cells' terminals and resistance spot-welding it to each cell, a standard way to join cylindrical cells into a pack (a pack maker's process note: Lithion Battery, "Resistance Welding for Cell Interconnect"; a 2022 study of tab welding to 18650 cells, Int. J. Adv. Manuf. Technol. 121:6581-6597). Each weld presses the welder's two copper tips onto the strip right over a terminal without knocking the pack apart; a missed weld leaves that cell out of the circuit.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Battery pack: an assembled 2x2 18650 pack, 41.2 x 41.2 x 68 mm, 201 g, loose on the table with its centre at (0.31, 0.03), sides along x and y: the bottom and top halves of a black ABS cell holder (the top one is the bottom one flipped over, pressed onto the cells) and four yellow 18 x 65 mm lithium-ion cells 20 mm apart, positive ends up, their + nubs 0.2 mm proud of the top face. Nickel strip: an H of 0.15 mm nickel, 28 x 28 mm, 1 g, two 8 mm bars joined by a bridge with a folded grip tab (8 mm wide, 10 mm tall, 3 mm across) in its middle, lying with its bars along x in a 40 x 40 x 8 mm grey tray fixed to the table at (0.27, -0.19). Spot welder: a handheld 18650 spot welder, black ABS housing 124 x 24 x 22 mm (138.7 mm long with its two copper probes, 127 g with its cell inside), seated in an orange PLA holder (142 x 39 x 14 mm, open at the middle of its long sides) screwed to the table with its centre at (0.30, 0.26), long axis along x, probes toward the robot.
scoring: Six steps, judged from the video. (1) Strip on the pack, 0.2: at the end the strip lies flat (within 10 degrees) on the cells' + nubs, its centre within 3 mm of the pack's, its bars over the cell pairs (within 10 degrees of a quarter turn), no gripper holds it, and a gripper took it out of its tray. (2-5) Cell 1, 2, 3, 4 welded, 0.1 each, once done: with the strip on the pack and the welder in a gripper, both probe tips touch the strip's metal (within 0.5 mm of its top face, not past its edges) over that cell's + terminal (within 3.5 mm of its axis) for 0.2 s; each weld leaves two dark spots on the strip. (6) Welder back in its holder, 0.2: at the end, after a gripper took it out, the welder sits in its holder's pocket (within 5 mm of its seat, on the floor within 2 mm, upright within 10 degrees) and no gripper holds it. On a real station a weld counts only if it bonded: after the run, a spring scale hooked under the strip beside that cell's weld pulls straight up at 10 N for 2 s, and the weld counts if the strip stays on that terminal. In simulation a weld is the touch alone. Full score 1.0, ending the run, only once all of these have held together without a break for 1 s: all six steps, both arms back where they started (within 3 cm) holding nothing, and the welder, the strip and the pack still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Any lapse, such as a part moving faster, restarts that second; until the second is complete, all six steps score 0.8. 0 overall if at the end the pack has been knocked over (tilted more than 20 degrees) or any part has fallen off the table.
reset_notes: Put the strip back in its tray, bars along x, tab up (a new strip if it shows weld spots); stand the pack back on its mark, top holder on, all cells positive end up; seat the welder in its holder, probes toward the robot, lid shut. A real trial uses a new strip and fresh, undamaged cells at storage charge.
fidelity: Articulated and rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The welder is one articulation (latched lid, latch slider, + contact) holding its cell. The pack is one rigid body (a press fit): holders as signed distance fields, cells as prisms. The 0.15 mm strip collides as 0.3 mm boxes, the probe tips as convex hulls ending in 0.22 mm balls. A weld is a 0.2 s touch that shows two dark spots where the tips touched: no current, heat or bond. No deformation.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (its arms reached toward the battery pack and the strip's tray again and again, but it never picked up the strip or took the welder out); demo: 1.0 (all six steps by step 939, success conditions from step 1024, 1.0 at step 1044)
